title: BatchReceipt
description: What the server returns from POST /v1/sessions/{id}/batches. Source: Terrastep plan section 16 and 17. A rejection is a reasoned verification outcome, NOT deletion of the user's personal record.

receipt_id.description: Canonical receipt. Retrying the same idempotency_key returns this same id.

state.description: accepted = fully credited. pending = evidence held for later verification. partial = some segments credited, some withheld. rejected = nothing credited. Plan section 17: commit the transaction BEFORE producing any client result that implies an award.

credited_minutes.description: Competitive minutes credited after caps. May legitimately be zero while the walk still counts as fitness. Plan section 10: explain this before the cap, without telling the person to keep exercising.

recorded_minutes.description: Total minutes recorded as personal fitness, capped or not. Recorded distance and ranked minutes can differ legitimately and the UI must explain why.

cells_affected.description: H3 cell IDs as TEXT. JavaScript cannot hold a 64-bit integer safely, so H3 ids are text at every API boundary. Plan section 15.

message.description: Plain language, safe to show the user. Never reveals detection thresholds - plan section 18 keeps those internal.

sequence.description: Which sample the reason applies to, when applicable.

reasons.description: Empty when state is accepted with nothing withheld. Never empty when state is rejected.

risk_state.description: Plan section 18: fitness_only means personal tracking continues but ranked awards pause. This is an explainable state with an appeal path, never a silent ban and never a public accusation.

allOf.$comment: A rejection or partial credit with no stated reason is an unexplained failure. Plan section 16: rejection is a reasoned verification outcome. The client cannot show the user anything useful without a reason, and nobody can debug without one.
